label: Bible Study
prompt: Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be _____, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.
verse: Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.
note: Discipline doesn't feel joyous at the time — the fruit comes afterward.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: When they saw the _____, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.
verse: When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.
note: The wise men had followed it a long way — when the star stood over the place, their joy ran over.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And she dwelt under the _____ tree of Deborah between Ramah and Beth-el in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.
verse: And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Beth-el in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.
note: Deborah held court under a palm tree in the hills of Ephraim — Israel's only woman judge, with an outdoor office.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And he shall _____ the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
verse: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.
note: The final verse of the Old Testament promises Elijah will come to turn hearts — Luke 1:17 applies it to John the Baptist.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: That which the _____ hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the cankerworm hath left hath the caterpiller eaten.
verse: That which the palmerworm hath left hath the locust eaten; and that which the locust hath left hath the cankerworm eaten; and that which the cankerworm hath left hath the caterpiller eaten.
note: Joel's plague comes in four waves — palmerworm, locust, cankerworm, caterpiller — and the KJV spells that last one oddly too.
